image:image.image:title: Research
image:image.image:caption: AI-driven neural time series network forecasting and cost analysis for dye removal prediction in packed bed adsorption using ultrasonic biomass composites for sustainable wastewater management Researchers at SIMATS Engineering have contributed to the field of wastewater treatment with their AI-driven neural time series network forecasting model for dye removal in packed bed adsorption systems. Their study, published in Environmental Research (2025), demonstrates an innovative approach to optimize performance and cost analysis for sustainable wastewater management.

image:image.image:title: Research
image:image.image:caption: Novelty of SESUS Research at SIMATS Engineering At SIMATS engineering, researchers are pioneering the future of energy storage and grid modernization through our groundbreaking research on the Swarm Energy Storage Unit System (SESUS). This innovative approach integrates nanoscale energy storage with swarm robotics, revolutionizing how power grids manage and distribute energy.

image:image.image:title: Research
image:image.image:caption: Green Hydrogen From Waste: Exploring the Promise of Sustainable Catalysis Research on converting industrial, agricultural, and municipal waste into nanocatalysts for green hydrogen production is carried out in SIMATS. Waste-derived catalysts deliver up to 30% higher yields with lower carbon footprints, supported by LCA studies. It examines applications, policies, and sustainability metrics, highlighting challenges and opportunities for scalable, circular-economy-driven solutions.

image:image.image:title: Research
image:image.image:caption: AI-Driven Biomass-Based Dye Remediation at SIMATS Engineering Researchers at SIMATS Engineering developed a novel mixed biomass from algae and Manila tamarind seeds for efficient dye adsorption, achieving 79.95 mg/g (EB) and 102.4 mg/g (BO) removal. The integration of AI models (ANN-PSO, ANFIS) significantly improved prediction accuracy (R² = 0.9999, 0.9994), enabling a sustainable and reusable solution for wastewater treatment.

image:image.image:title: Research
image:image.image:caption: Advancements in MIS Schottky Barrier Diodes at SIMATS Engineering Researchers at SIMATS Engineering explored Metal-Insulator-Semiconductor (MIS) Schottky barrier diodes, focusing on material selection, fabrication techniques, and device performance. The study highlights JNSP thin film coating as a cost-effective, non-toxic approach and demonstrates the potential of transition metals for advanced optoelectronic applications.
